fixes.explanation: That's the text, baker. After He had dismissed the crowds, He “…went up on the mountain by Himself to pray.” (Matthew 14:23). He heads up to be alone and pray. I'd have gone straight for a nap.

Here's what the text says, friend. After He had dismissed the crowds, Jesus “…went up on the mountain by Himself to pray.” (Matthew 14:23). So He does go up the mountain, and He goes alone. It's all right there in the verse.

Yes, the wind. The text says the boat was “…buffeted by the waves because the wind was against it.” (Matthew 14:24). Rowing into a wind like that is like walking into a gust with your umbrella open. You push forward and it pushes right back.

That's it. “…Jesus went out to them, walking on the sea.” (Matthew 14:25). He's out on top of the water, headed toward the disciples in their boat. That all happens during the fourth watch of the night.
That's what they say. “It’s a ghost!” and they cry out in fear (Matthew 14:26). It's the fourth watch of the night and somebody is walking on the water. I'm not sure what else I'd have yelled either.
An angel would be a nicer thing to see, baker, but that isn't what they say. The disciples are terrified and say, “It’s a ghost!” (Matthew 14:26). So the word they use is ghost.

Yes. Peter, one of the disciples, says, “Lord, if it is You, command me to come to You on the water” (Matthew 14:28). He doesn't ask for a smoother sea. He asks to come out to Jesus. That's a big ask with the wind blowing like that.

True! Peter “…got down out of the boat, walked on the water, and came toward Jesus.” (Matthew 14:29). He actually walked on it. I'd have stared at that water for an hour before I hopped off on my gold base.
Yes, immediately. “Immediately Jesus reached out His hand and took hold of Peter.” (Matthew 14:31). Peter was beginning to sink when that happened (Matthew 14:30). That's what I'd call a quick hand.

The text doesn't give Jesus any reluctance, friend. It says “Immediately Jesus reached out His hand and took hold of Peter.” (Matthew 14:31). That word tells us how He answers Peter beginning to sink (Matthew 14:30).

Right, it's when they're back in the boat. “…when they had climbed back into the boat, the wind died down.” (Matthew 14:32). That's the moment the text gives for the wind dying down. I think that's worth noticing.

That's a fair guess, baker, but the text doesn't say Jesus speaks to the wind here. It says “…when they had climbed back into the boat, the wind died down.” (Matthew 14:32). So that's the moment the text gives.

Yes, worshiped. The text says “…those who were in the boat worshiped Him…” (Matthew 14:33). Earlier the disciples were terrified and cried out, “It’s a ghost!” (Matthew 14:26). I think that's a big change.
That's it, Son. They say, “Truly You are the Son of God!” (Matthew 14:33). It's one of the biggest things said on that boat all night. They're calling Jesus the Son of God.
Not at all. The men of that place recognized Jesus and “…sent word to all the surrounding region.” (Matthew 14:35). So they don't keep it to themselves. Then people brought all the sick to Him.
Yes. They “…begged Him just to let them touch the fringe of His cloak.” (Matthew 14:36). That's what the people ask for. I think it's a humble thing to ask.

The text doesn't say they ask Him to come home with them, friend. They “…begged Him just to let them touch the fringe of His cloak.” (Matthew 14:36). Their request is about touching the fringe of His cloak.
True, all of them. “…all who touched Him were healed.” (Matthew 14:36). The text says all, not most and not some. That's the word to hold on to.
Here's what the text says, friend. “…all who touched Him were healed.” (Matthew 14:36). Everyone who touched Him was healed, and nobody gets left out. So the statement is true as written.
